body.x: Three Hi Seoul companies participated in K-Startup Joint Pavilion in Eureka Park, the start-up zone of “CES 2023” hosted in Las Vegas, U.S., for four days from Thursday, January 5 to Sunday, January 8, 2023 in local time.

Hi Seoul companies are promising SMEs based in Seoul that are certified by the Seoul Metropolitan Government and Seoul Business Agency since 2004. As of 2022, 1,059 businesses have been certified after having gone through annual expert reviews based on their growth, technological competence, and potential to enter overseas markets. They are also considered to be leading Seoul's economy with achievements such as becoming listed on KOSDAQ, securing government assignments, and increasing sales.

In fact, with average sales of 13.6 billion won and an average of 51.3 employees, they have 2.5 times the average sales and number of employees compared to the average for venture companies. Moreover, half of Hi Seoul companies are export companies, and the average company operation period is 17 years. As of last October, 41 Hi Seoul businesses have successfully been listed on KOSDAQ. The top industries were information and communication (IT) (23.8%), followed by business services (22.5%).

At this year's CES, three of the members—Nuvilab (AI food scan solution), Xinapse (AI virtual voice service), and AIZEN Global (AI finance solution)—joined the K-startup Joint Pavilion in Eureka Park.
Global media channel Aving News interviewed Hyun-hae Park, head of the Hi Seoul company team, on the 5th (local time), the first day of CES.

Q. Choe: This year, CES is taking place in the midst of the endemic. While last year's event took place both online and offline due to the COVID19 pandemic, this year's event is now offline again at its original size. How do you find the atmosphere on the site?

A. Park: The most well-known exhibition lives up to the expectations. Eureka Park is clustered with start-ups, and the LVCC hall, the main exhibition hall of CES, is flooded with people. This means that many companies, buyers, and visitors interested in related areas have been waiting for today.
Q. Choe: Could you tell us a bit about Hi Seoul companies?

A. Park: Promising businesses in Seoul have been screened based on the city’s Promising SME Certification Support Ordinance to be certified as Hi Seoul members and 1,059 businesses have been certified so far. They are of these businesses in various lines of work and industries. The model in which these diverse companies come together to create synergy and continue to develop through cooperation and coexistence would be the biggest driving force behind Hi-Seoul companies.
Q. Choe: Could you introduce the three member companies participating in CES 2023?

A. Park: Eureka Park, where the Hi Seoul participants have set up their booths, is a place run mainly by start-ups. There used to be a lot of manufacturers, whereas the latest trend is that companies with non-face-to-face tech and solutions are standing out. In line with this trend, all three CES participants own artificial intelligence (AI)-related technology.

body.cap: Joseph Choe, editor-in-chief of Aving News (left), interviewing Hyun-hae Park, head of the Hi Seoul company team (right) at AIZEN Global's booth in Eureka Park, Venetian Expo Center in Las Vegas, U.S. on the 5th (local time) | Photo by Aving News

body.x: Among them, AIZEN Global has contributed to the global transition to a low-carbon future and green financing through CreditConnect, its AI Banking-as-a-Service platform. Notably, it predicts the residual value of previously non-measurable electric batteries and transparently measures associated financial risks to create new financial opportunities in the EV (Electric Vehicle) industry.

Since the first launch of CreditConnect BEV in South Korea in 2022, the start-up has partnered with Korean battery platform businesses to develop an ML-based battery residual value prediction system using real-time battery data, providing the funds to purchase more than 150 electric buses. Sharing the challenges and opportunities faced by the U.S. on the transition to EV, AIZEN Global has high hopes for this year's CES where they hope to find potential partners to create a global EV ecosystem together.

Furthermore, AI food scanning solution developer Nuvilab is presenting its healthcare concept based on diet data at this year's CES. With its mobile app and API embedded with the food data that Nuvilab's AI has studied for four years, it is expected that the firm will introduce a new future for various user environments in the field of digital healthcare.

body.cap: NuviLab's exclusive booth in the Digital Health Zone at Las Vegas Convention Center North Hall │ Photo by Aving News

body.x: NuviLab has gained attention at home and abroad by developing solutions that innovate group meal cooking environments using technology to identify the types and quantities of food with a single scan. The CES 2023 attendee is collaborating with Eun-ha Kim, an emerging installation artist, to promote its influence on the formation of healthy eating habits and protection of the global environment.

Lastly, Xinapse is an AI voice technology-based generative AI start-up with a variety of AI voice variation skills which grants the company flexible scalability. In this exhibition, the company introduced HyperReal Voice, its software for professionals that helps them easily and quickly create customized AI virtual voice content. Customers can easily create natural AI voices that resemble human voices by simply typing in text, and they can control the emotion, pitch, and speed of the voice with just a few mouse clicks and drags.

There are many cases where great ideas go to waste because people can't focus on content due to lack of capital. Xinapse is working on technologies that will allow people to create content with less cost and time so that more people can focus on ideas and content instead of capital.

body.x: These three companies are promoting their excellent artificial intelligence technologies and seeking global business as CES 2023 participants.
Q. Choe: I know that Hi Seoul companies announced their vision based on the concept of “Companionship” at the end of last year. Could you explain what it is about?

A. Park: On December 14, 2022, in the presence of Seoul Mayor Se-Hoon Oh, we declared the 2023 vision of the Hi Seoul companies under the theme of “Special City with Attractive Companionship.” This vision is made up of three main parts.

First, we have companionship with the vulnerable. This shows the willingness of Hi Seoul companies to stand by the marginalized people in our society. Second, there's companionship with ESG. Although the term ESG may still sound unfamiliar in Korea, in other developed countries around the world, there are already norms established for ESG. These have been put in place both institutionally and legally. In light of this, Hi Seoul has plans to conduct ESG management in accordance with international standards.

Lastly, we have a vision for companionship with the world. Hi Seoul companies export approximately 3 trillion KRW to 98 countries. About 500 of the 1,059 companies are exporters, and it is our goal to help the rest of them expand into the global market. That is why we chose companionship with the world as our keyword for the vision.
Q. Choe: It seems like you're going to be very busy this year to work on this vision. What are your plans for this year?

A. Park: We're planning quite a number of events to create opportunities for our companies to continue to expand overseas. We will be dispatching delegations not just to exhibitions but also to major cities around the world to arrange meetings with major buyers or potential partners. The World Korean Business Convention will be held this October in Orange County, USA. The Hi Seoul delegation will be attending the event to form various partnerships and hold business meetings with Korean American businesses and major buyers.

Meanwhile, CES, the world's largest IT fair, is an exhibition that provides a comprehensive view of the global consumer electronics industry in one place. It is held annually in Las Vegas in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). Aving News has annually reported on CES news for the world for 17 consecutive years since 2006, hosting the Best of CES, which selects the best innovative products and technologies, and the Best of Made in Korea, which chooses the most innovative businesses in South Korea. In addition, the media has delivered breaking news about CES through AVING LIVE.
